holidays.name: National Eat Outside Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to taking your meals out of the dining room and into the fresh air. Picnics, backyard barbecues, and sidewalk sandwiches are all fair game, ants and unpredictable breezes included.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States as an unofficial food-and-lifestyle holiday, it reportedly grew out of end-of-summer traditions of squeezing in a few last outdoor meals before fall arrives.
holidays.funFact: Studies on dining environments suggest that people often report enjoying food more when eating outdoors, and a sandwich eaten on a park bench really does feel fancier.

holidays.name: National Trail Mix Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the snack that combines nuts, dried fruit, seeds, and often chocolate into one portable pouch of joy. It's also the unofficial day to argue about whether raisins belong in the mix.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday in the United States, it falls at the end of summer, the peak of hiking and camping season, which makes it a natural fit for a day honoring hiker fuel.
holidays.funFact: Trail mix is often called 'gorp,' which some people claim stands for 'Good Old Raisins and Peanuts,' though the term's real origin is debated and may predate that backronym.

holidays.name: Love Litigating Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek observance for people who adore arguments, legal wrangling, and the fine art of building a case. Lawyers, debate nerds, and anyone who 'just wants to clarify one thing' are invited to celebrate.
holidays.origin: This is a lesser-known, informal observance and its exact origin is unclear. It appears in various listings of offbeat holidays and plays on the joys of the legal profession.
holidays.funFact: The word 'litigate' comes from the Latin 'litigare,' meaning 'to dispute or quarrel,' which is basically the same energy as a family road trip.

holidays.name: International Overdose Awareness Day
holidays.description: A global day of remembrance and awareness. It honors those lost to overdose, supports grieving families, and aims to reduce stigma around drug-related deaths while promoting prevention and harm reduction.
holidays.origin: Started in 2001 by Sally Finn at The Salvation Army in Melbourne, Australia, as a way to remember people lost to overdose and to spark conversation. It has since grown into a worldwide observance.
holidays.funFact: Purple ribbons and silver badges are symbols of the day, and many landmarks around the world light up in purple to mark it.

holidays.name: Frankenstein Friday Adjacent: Mary Shelley Monster Mash Moment (World Frankenstein Day Run-Up)
holidays.description: A playful pop culture nod to Mary Shelley, born on August 30, whose famous novel gave the world its most misunderstood monster. Fans celebrate by watching classic monster movies and arguing that Frankenstein is the doctor, not the creature.
holidays.origin: This is a fan-driven, informal extension of the celebration of Mary Shelley's birthday on August 30, and it spills over into the following day for monster movie marathons.
holidays.funFact: Mary Shelley began writing Frankenstein at just 18 years old, during a ghost-story challenge among friends on a gloomy summer holiday in Switzerland.
